relationship: Proposed identity of the divine book
rationale: Both texts mention God’s book, but Exodus concerns blotting out a sinner while the psalm combines unworked substance, writing and formation over days with unresolved referents. The same named book or registry is not established.

relationship: Proposed identification of the overshadowed head with salvation’s helmet
rationale: The psalm names protection of the speaker’s head in war; Isaiah has the Lord place a helmet of salvation on His own head. The psalm does not name a helmet, and the different wearer prevents the proposed exact armor identification.

relationship: Proposed identification of David’s cave occasion
rationale: The psalm heading names a cave but no location or pursuer. Samuel records David in the En-gedi cave and also records the Adullam cave in 22:1. This target does not uniquely establish the heading’s occasion.

General kingdom, glory and authority vocabulary does not establish a sufficiently particular relationship between speaking of God’s kingdom and the vision of bestowed authority. This removed original draft pair has zero credit; the more specific enduring-kingdom relation at 144:13 is separate.

relationship: Proposed equivalence of making the blind wise and recovery of sight
rationale: Psalm 145 says the Lord makes the blind wise, whereas Isaiah’s commissioned speaker proclaims recovery of sight to the blind. Treating these as the same healing action would erase the source’s wisdom wording. The retained raising-of-the-broken comparison is independent.

relationship: Proposed historical identification of Jerusalem’s secured gates
rationale: The psalm praises God for strengthening gate bars and blessing the city’s children. Nehemiah narrates doors set up, wedged fast and guarded, without identifying the psalm or its blessing. The precise historical equation remains unresolved.

relationship: Proposed identification of the written judgment
rationale: The psalm does not name the written judgment. Deuteronomy’s divine sword, vengeance and repayment provide context for the separately retained 149:7 comparison, but do not identify the unspecified writing in 149:9.

relationship: Proposed identity of the sent angel with Samuel
rationale: The psalm says He sent His angel; the narrative names Samuel as the one anointing David. The supported sheep-to-anointing comparison does not prove that angel denotes Samuel, and that identity receives no additional credit.
